description: The bar chart illustrates the results of human evaluations comparing three language models—Claude3.5, GPT4o, and Doubao—across three outcome categories: Win, Tie, and Lose, as part of the ChARM framework for character-based act-adaptive reward modeling in role-playing agents. The horizontal axis represents the proportion of evaluations ranging from 0.0 to 1.0 (or 0% to 100%), while the vertical axis lists the three models. Each model’s performance is visualized as a stacked horizontal bar divided into three colored segments: pink for “Win,” light blue for “Tie,” and light green for “Lose,” with percentage values labeled within each segment. For Claude3.5, the distribution is 32.0% Win, 44.0% Tie, and 24.0% Lose. GPT4o shows 56.0% Win, 18.0% Tie, and 26.0% Lose, indicating a strong preference in human evaluations. Doubao scores 42.0% Win, 36.0% Tie, and 22.0% Lose. The chart visually emphasizes GPT4o’s higher win rate and lower tie rate compared to the others, while Claude3.5 has the highest tie rate. The legend at the bottom clearly maps the colors to the outcome categories, and all values are presented as percentages with one decimal place.
